name: Heddle Loft

stars.name: Heddle A
stars.notes: Brilliant young main-sequence star whose ultraviolet flood sterilizes every orbit close to it.

stars.name: Heddle B
stars.notes: Companion 110 AU out; cool enough to host the system's only sheltered worlds, which orbit it as a private hearth away from A's glare.

planets.name: Glasswake
planets.notes: S-type orbit of Heddle A; surface fused to a mirror glaze by proximity to the white star, used as an optical calibration target.

planets.name: Whitekiln
planets.notes: S-type orbit of Heddle A; tidal and radiative heating keep lava seas open, mined by teleoperated crucible rigs for exotic basalts.

planets.name: Stonecreel
planets.notes: S-type orbit of Heddle A at the outer edge of the burn zone; a wound-scarred rock where Consortium survey beacons outnumber boulders.

planets.name: Softacre
planets.notes: Inhabited S-type world of Heddle B in its comfortable habitable band; warm shallow seas support the charter's kelp-farming colony of forty thousand.

planets.name: Barleymow
planets.notes: S-type orbit of Heddle B beside Softacre; dry-grass steppes reserved by charter for expansion once the ocean farms plateau.

planets.name: Windrow
planets.notes: Outermost S-type planet of Heddle B; dust seas harvested by drone caravans for rare-earth pans.

planets.name: Warpwind
planets.notes: First circumbinary P-type world, circling both stars beyond the cleared boundary; its fuel scaffold anchors all deep-system logistics.

planets.name: Frostfleece
planets.notes: P-type ice giant ringed by volatile moons; long-range tanker route terminus for the outer dark.

planets.name: Nineply
planets.notes: Outermost P-type wanderer on a tilted wide orbit; a beacon here warns ships away from the unstable seam between the stars' Hill spheres.

asteroid_belts.name: The Shed Line
asteroid_belts.notes: The chaotic seam between B's S-type family and the circumbinary zone was swept clean early, leaving this thin residue that Consortium drones still resurvey each decade.

stations.name: Loftsman Terminal
stations.notes: Charter-run port above Softacre handling kelp exports, immigration quotas, and every berth fee in the system.

stations.name: Charterhouse Ring
stations.notes: Rotating research ring studying A-star radiation effects and long-duration habitat design; its findings set Consortium construction code.

stations.name: Warpwind Fuel Scaffold
stations.notes: He-3 skimming gantry complex feeding outbound tankers; the hardest-working structure in the system.

faction_control.notes: A corporate charter governs the entire binary under century-lease; colonists hold tenant rights on Softacre and little else.

history: The young binary was flagged during a luminosity census as a hazard corridor until scouts found the temperate waters around Heddle B.
The Heddlehold Consortium bought the survey debt outright and planted Softacre Colony within twenty years, importing kelp genome stock from three older agri-worlds.
Renewal hearings now underway on the charter have drawn settler lobbyists, rival combines, and at least two intelligence services to Loftsman Terminal.
description: A white A-class furnace dominates Heddle Loft, blazing over three scorched inner worlds, while its yellow-white companion waits far out like a banked hearth with a family gathered round. Everything inside the burn zone is glass and lava; everything near Heddle B is steppe and warm sea. One thin belt of rubble marks the seam where neither star's dominion is quite safe.

The Heddlehold Consortium owns the lease on all of it, and forty thousand colonists raise kelp beneath B's steadier light at Softacre. Freighters cycle between the fuel scaffold at Warpwind and the export terminals overhead, keeping traffic steady but orderly. Researchers at Charterhouse Ring quietly shape how half the sector builds habitats.

The charter renewal has opened old questions about who actually owns a tide. Settler delegates argue the lease lapsed in spirit when the original signatory combine collapsed, and their lawyers are better than expected. Meanwhile Nineply's warning beacon has begun logging unregistered transits through the seam, and nobody filing those flight plans answers to the Consortium.
